title: a value the page keeps beneath is never the owner's choice
line: Charlotte's 1900 household page shows Norriton Township and keeps Norristown beneath it; beside the file's 1900 Residence at Norristown she carries two more of that year with no place, so neither place the page gives fits one of them alone: the place it shows is a question for the owner, the place it keeps beneath is none, since it is never accepted, never ground and never a conflict; placed by the owner all the same, it is written undecided and marked, never accepted with the record, while the place the page shows, placed, is accepted with it

steps.say: the 1900 Lukens household page, on the owner's word that it is Charlotte's
a second Residence of 1900 the harness plants beside the file's, with no place
the owner accepts her card on it: neither place the page gives lands on one Residence of its year

expect.why: one question, for the place the page shows (it fits the two placeless Residences equally); the place it keeps beneath fits three equally, yet nothing asks the owner to place it: where it stands decides nothing

question.detail_has: fits 2 of your 5 residence events equally

expect.why: the one question is the shown place's

steps.say: the owner places the place kept beneath on the first placeless Residence all the same

expect.why: what the page also says is kept and cited, never accepted with the record
undecided, as an acceptance writes the place kept beneath where the event is plain

steps.say: and the place the page shows on the second

expect.why: the shown place accepted with the record, the place kept beneath undecided
